subject: Proposed Food Truck Ordinance Restructuring
overview: The committee met to refine a proposed food truck ordinance, moving toward a structure that delegates operational permitting to the Board of Health while retaining city oversight for the use of public ways. The body aims to streamline one-day and special event permits while maintaining protections for established brick-and-mortar businesses.

items.title: Food Truck Ordinance Review
items.summary: The committee discussed updating a 2016 food truck policy into a formal ordinance to clarify permitting processes for mobile vendors.

items.title: Regulatory Framework and Legal Recommendations
items.summary: Attorney Robin Stein of KP Law recommended splitting the proposal into Board of Health regulations for food safety and sanitary operations and city ordinances for land use and permissions to use public streets.

items.title: Protection of Brick-and-Mortar Businesses
items.summary: Councilors emphasized that permits should be restricted to one-day or special event licenses to prevent mobile vendors from competing with permanent restaurant businesses.

items.title: Administrative Permitting Authority
items.summary: The committee debated delegating the authority to grant locations on public ways from the City Council to administrative departments to expedite the application process.

items.title: Zoning and Revenue Considerations
items.summary: Members discussed how the new regulations would interact with existing brewery zoning and confirmed that mobile vendors are subject to local meals taxes.

items.title: Drafting Instructions and Legal Billing
items.summary: The committee approved a motion for legal counsel and staff to return with separate ordinance and regulation drafts, as well as a request for a report on legal fees associated with the drafting process.
